surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption and desorption of Cd and Te atoms during ALE growth. The Cd-spot intensity is a direct measure of Cd surface coverage, while the Te-spot intensity reflects Te coverage. The intensity variations are explained by adsorption models, where the Cd-spot intensity increases linearly with time during Cd-deposition, and the Te-spot intensity follows an exponential model during Te-deposition. The intensity drop of the Cd-spot upon Te-deposition suggests that Te coverage inhibits Cd-related surface resonance conditions.
evidence: During Cd-deposition the intensity of the Cd-spot increases linearly with time up to a saturation value. The dotted line marked 'model 1' is the Cd surface coverage calculated from the known Cd beam intensity under the simple assumption that every impinging Cd atom sticks at the surface. During Te-deposition the Te-spot increases, but not proportional to the offered Te flux. The time until the saturation value of the Te-spot is reached, is much longer than for the Cd-spot, although the Cd-and Te-fluxes are comparable. If one considers that Te adsorbs presumably as large and compared to Cd immobile Te2-molecules, that cannot easily change their sites if hit by further Te2-particles, it seems reasonable to assume that Te2-molecules stick only if they hit empty surface sites and re-evaporate if they hit occupied ones.
